time_value_disclaimer.note: The fixed sentence after a time-value figure, on 11 en keys (achievements.badge.{clockedIn,wageDay,wageHour,wageMonth,wageQuarter,wageWeek,wageYear}.earned, achievements.category.wages.description, widgets.cash.description, widgets.focusRing.a11y.money, widgets.monthlyTimeValue.description). references/locale-briefs/de.md '## Money frame' fixes this exact form and says it mirrors this glossary entry exactly. forecast.note: The month-end projection of time value (insights.savings.forecast, insights.savings.*EstimateExplanation, insights.appUsage.permissionDescription, widgets.monthlyTimeValue.*). The brief does not narrate this concept in prose, so it is seeded directly as nl.json and fi.json seed it, rather than sent to Open decisions as ro.md does for its own equivalent term: unlike ro's shipped 3/3 split, no de copy exists, and German keeps the forecast line and the month-end estimate apart without effort ('Prognose' for the forward-looking figure, 'Schätzung' for insights.savings.monthEnd and .estimated), so VoiceOver's back-to-back read of the two needs two distinct words the way the ro open decision requires an owner call to get. forbidden mirrors glossary/concepts.json 'forecast' not_this (prediction, promise, guaranteed amount): 'Versprechen' and 'Garantie' would turn an estimate into a claim, and 'Garantie' already backs the brief's own Money frame ban on 'guaranteed' (grep stem 'garant', 0 en keys), so this row reinforces that ban rather than duplicating it on a different word.

hourly_rate.note: The rate the user sets to price their own time (onboarding.hourlyWage.*, profile.hourlyWage.*, currency.settings.*, screenTimeReport.missingWage, achievements.category.wages.description). references/locale-briefs/de.md '## Control forms' and '## Header and label forms' ship 'Set Your Hourly Wage' -> 'Lege deinen Stundensatz fest' (onboarding.hourlyWage.title), and '## Header and label forms' lists 'der Stundensatz' among the gender-agreement examples. 'Stundenlohn' and 'Gehalt' are forbidden because the en source itself says wage in three places this term governs (onboarding.hourlyWage.title 'Set Your Hourly Wage', .footer 'hourly rate', screenTimeReport.missingWage 'your hourly wage'), which is exactly the word a translator reaches for and exactly wrong, because the app pays nobody. The badge family's payroll vocabulary ('Lohnliste', 'Schicht', references/locale-briefs/de.md '## Idioms and figurative language') is a metaphor built from a different compound and does not collide with 'Stundenlohn'.

daily_focus_goal.note: The daily minutes target drawn as a ring, met or not met (onboarding.dailyFocusGoal.*, profile.focusTarget.*, widgets.focusRing.*). references/locale-briefs/de.md '## Header and label forms' lists 'das Ziel' among the gender-agreement examples, and '## Audience and register' / '## Decided conflicts' settle closed-compound spelling for this kind of noun ('Bildschirmzeit', 'Fokussitzung'), which 'Tagesziel' follows. forbidden is empty on purpose: onboarding.personalGoal.* and the quote surfaces legitimately need 'Ziel'-family words for an aspiration, a different sense the concept's own not_this ('aim, aspiration, life goal') keeps separate, so banning the bare noun would fire on correct copy.

minute_unit.note: The compact minute unit, spaced by default and glued only on a render verdict (common.durationMinuteUnit, insights.sessions.durationMinuteUnit, widgets.startFocus.minuteUnit, share.duration.minutesOnly, screenTimeReport.durationMinutesOnly, widgets.streak.focusedInStreak, widgets.streak.focusedMinutesSummary, moneyfesting.details.timeElapsedFormat, component.templateTaskCard.duration). references/locale-briefs/de.md '## Short forms and units' and '## Decided conflicts' settle 'Min.' from Foundation's de_DE abbreviated duration output ('1 Std., 45 Min.'), with the bare narrow multi-letter form reserved for the share-card compact triple, itself a seed (share.duration.minutesShort). forbidden is empty because the drift form is the single letter 'm', and a one-letter forbidden entry would fire on anything; a bare 'm' left over from en outside the share card is an editor finding recorded in the brief's Short forms table, not a forbidden glossary entry.

Keys: widgets.streak.smallHeader, .currentStreakHeader, .displayName, .daysCount, .dayStreakCount, insights.summary.dayStreakTitle, share.card.streakEyebrow, achievements.streak.title, onboarding.welcome.slide.streak.{eyebrow,headline}, paywall.benefit.streak.title, the whole streakFreeze.* family. Evidence per option: 'Serie' is the plain German noun (5 characters), used generically for a winning or losing streak in sport, and takes a compound ('Serienwidget'), with no Apple evidence for this exact sense found in this harvest (a gap, unlike nl's and ro's Fitness-bundle citations for their own equivalent nouns); 'Tage in Folge' is a plain phrase, natural in running text, but cannot fill a header or a compact compound; 'Streak' is the English loan some German apps use and is ruled out by the no-English-needed rule. Decide before the first de batch; a flip afterwards is a global term change with its own follow-up batch.

open.recommended_reason: 'Frost' fails as the countable noun the badge/inventory copy needs: it is ordinarily an uncountable weather noun and its rare plural 'Fröste' reads oddly as a UI count, and a web check for how German speakers discuss the identical Duolingo mechanic surfaced only a verb phrase, never a coined noun like 'Frost'; a compound such as 'Frostschutz' or 'Serienschutz' should be tested with a native reviewer before the pilot instead.
open.note: No de copy exists. Keys: the 12 streakFreeze.* keys, widgets.streak.copy.frozen.*, widgets.streak.a11y.frozen, paywall.benefit.streak.detail. Rule: keep the 'frozen' image the source relies on, in everyday German a reader without English understands, and still work as a countable noun where badge/inventory copy needs one. Evidence per option: 'Frost' is a short punchy noun that fits a one-word widget label and pairs with the verb phrase 'die Serie einfrieren', but is a pure agent proposal with no Apple string or other verified precedent, and is ordinarily uncountable in German ('Fröste' as a plural count reads oddly); 'Frostschutz'/'Serienschutz' are compounds built the way German normally coins a countable protection-noun, avoiding the countability problem at the cost of being longer and still uncited; 'Serie einfrieren' as a verb-only option avoids coining a noun German does not already have for this sense, at the cost of leaving badge and inventory labels that need a countable noun without a clean short form; 'Streak-Freeze' is the English loan some fitness and language-learning apps keep, ruled out for the same reason as the streak noun itself. Meanwhile agents mark every use of 'Frost'/'Frostschutz' as a proposal and list every key touched, so a flip is one recorded change. This item exists because the evidence for a de streak-freeze word is weaker than for streak_term itself, not because the concept is any less settled elsewhere in the brief.

Rule: one conceit per locale, decided once and kept across the family, gender-neutral, with plain descriptors left plain. Evidence per option: keep it draws on German vocabulary with no gendered agent nouns at all ('Eingestempelt', 'Eingestellt', 'Auf Gehalt', 'Wieder angeheuert', 'Zurück im Dienst', 'Festangestellt', 'Doppelschicht', 'Die Lohnliste', 'Die Schicht', 'Dienstjahre'); drop it replaces the employment names with plain achievement names ('Erste Sitzung', 'Sieben Tage in Folge', 'Fünfzig volle Tage'), losing the wink but removing any reading of the app as an employer next to a money frame that already says five times that nothing is earned. Meanwhile the first achievements batch drafts the conceit, marks every name a proposal, and the adjudicator reports the whole family together so a flip is one batch.

open.recommended_reason: The entire purpose of a mock alert is to look identical to the real one, and a visible mismatch on the one button most likely to be compared side by side with the device undermines that purpose.
open.note: Key: common.continue, shared by the generic Continue control and quoted inside onboarding.alert.screenTimeMessage to describe the mock Screen Time alert's own button. Rule: a string that mocks an iOS alert equals Apple's value verbatim (references/locale-briefs/de.md Platform terms, Verbatim rule). Evidence: iOS 26.1 (23B86) runtime, UIKitCore.framework | Localizable.strings | Continue gives 'Weiter'; FamilyControlsAuthenticationUI.app | Localizable.strings | COMMON_CONTINUE gives 'Fortfahren' for the same concept in the Screen Time access alert specifically — the two Apple frameworks disagree with each other in German, unlike in Dutch, where they happened to coincide, so this finding is de-specific. Options: keep the single shared key accepts a small mismatch against the mocked alert's own wording with no code change; adding a dedicated key is a faithful mock at the cost of a new catalog key and call-site change (an engineering ask). Meanwhile: ship the shared key as 'Weiter' and record the mismatch in the report; do not add the key without the owner.

open.recommended_reason: Both the Germany and Austria App Store storefronts already default to German, unlike Belgium's English-first default in the Dutch case, so there is less risk that Germany-first vocabulary reads as wrong in Austria rather than merely unfamiliar.
open.note: Affects vocabulary across the catalog, not any single key. Rule: one de resource serves both audiences, because de-DE and de-AT both negotiate to de and iOS ships only de.lproj (apple-coverage system_negotiation). Evidence per option: Germany wording follows the larger market and iOS's own de.lproj, which reads as standard German rather than Austrian German throughout this harvest; Austria-aware wording would check the handful of terms Austrian German spells or uses differently before the first batch, though this app does not currently write any of the classic Germany/Austria vocabulary pairs (month names, foodstuffs) as literal copy, so the practical risk is smaller than the Dutch brief's Netherlands/Belgium item. Meanwhile: write Germany German, and record any term an editor flags as Austria-divergent in the batch report rather than hedging the line.
